extracted.intended_audience: researchers applying for Brain & Behavior Research Foundation (BBRF) grants / mental health researchers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and criteria for applying to BBRF research grants (Young Investigator, Independent Investigator, Distinguished Investigator), including eligibility, project relevance, funding amounts, and program intent for investigators at different career stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: BBRF Young Investigator Grant — eligibility and project relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: The BBRF Young Investigator Grant provides support for the most promising young scientists conducting neurobiological research. Two-year awards up to $70,000, or $35,000 per year are provided to enable promising investigators to either extend research fellowship training or begin careers as independent research faculty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basic and/or clinical investigators are supported, but research must be relevant to serious brain and behavior disorders such as schizophrenia, mood disorders, anxiety disorders or child and adolescent mental illnesses. See the 2026 YI Grant application guidelines and the stated acceptance periods for application timing. Contact grants@bbrfoundation.org for questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: BBRF Independent Investigator Grant — eligibility and project relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: The BBRF Independent Investigator Grant provides support for investigators during the critical period between the initiation of research and the receipt of sustained funding. A two-year grant up to $100,000 or $50,000 per year is provided to scientists at the associate professor level or equivalent who are clearly independent and have won national competitive support as a principal investigator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An assistant professor who is a principal investigator on a NIH R01 grant is now eligible for the BBRF Independent Investigator Grant. Basic and/or clinical investigators are supported, but research must be relevant to schizophrenia, major affective disorders, or other serious mental illnesses. The program is intended to facilitate innovative research opportunities. Application guidelines are subject to change; monitor the website or join the email list for acceptance period updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: BBRF Distinguished Investigator Grant — eligibility and project focus
rubrics_metrics.description: The BBRF Distinguished Investigator Grant provides support for experienced investigators (full professor or equivalent) conducting neurobiological and behavioral research. A one-year grant of $100,000 is provided for established scientists pursuing innovative projects in diverse areas of neurobiological research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Areas of particular interest to the Scientific Council's Selection Committee include patient populations with unique or unusual characteristics and central nervous system developments. See the DI Grant Application Guidelines and specified acceptance periods; contact grants@bbrfoundation.org with questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project relevance to serious brain and behavior disorders
rubrics_metrics.description: Across BBRF grant types, supported research must be relevant to serious brain and behavior disorders (examples given include schizophrenia, mood disorders, anxiety disorders, child and adolescent mental illnesses, major affective disorders, or other serious mental illnesses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should explicitly link proposed research to these disorder areas and to the Foundation's mission of understanding and treating mental illness. Both basic and clinical research are eligible when relevance is clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with Foundation priority areas
rubrics_metrics.description: BBRF funding is focused on four priority areas to better understand and treat mental illness: BASIC RESEARCH, NEW TECHNOLOGIES, DIAGNOSTIC TOOLS / EARLY INTERVENTIONS, NEXT-GENERATION THERAPIES.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications that clearly address one or more of these priority areas are favored. Applicants should describe how the proposed work advances understanding, diagnosis, early intervention, technology, or therapies for mental illnesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection emphasis: promise, innovation, and potential for breakthroughs
rubrics_metrics.description: All Grant application submissions are reviewed by the Scientific Council which reviews and selects the most promising research ideas with the greatest potential to lead to advancements and breakthroughs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should emphasize novelty, scientific promise, and potential impact toward advancements or breakthroughs. Evidence of feasibility and a convincing argument for substantial future impact will align with the Council's selection priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career-stage appropriateness and program intent
rubrics_metrics.description: Each BBRF grant type is intended for a specific career stage and purpose: Young Investigator grants to extend fellowship training or begin independent careers; Independent Investigator grants to support investigators between project initiation and sustained funding; Distinguished Investigator grants to support established investigators pursuing innovative work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should apply to the grant type appropriate to their career stage and demonstrate how the award will serve the stated program intent (e.g., launching an independent career, bridging to sustained funding, enabling high-impact innovative research).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility evidence: independence and prior competitive support (Independent Investigator criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Independent Investigator applicants must be clearly independent (associate professor level or equivalent) and have won national competitive support as a principal investigator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentary evidence of independence and prior competitive funding as PI (e.g., prior grants, leadership of projects) strengthens applications. Note that certain assistant professors (e.g., PI on an NIH R01) may qualify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding amounts, durations, and procedural application windows
rubrics_metrics.description: The grants specify award amounts and durations (e.g., YI: up to $70,000 over two years [$35,000/year]; Independent: up to $100,000 over two years [$50,000/year]; Distinguished: $100,000 for one year). The page lists acceptance periods for particular cycles and links to grant application guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must follow current application guidelines (which are subject to change), submit within the stated acceptance period, and use provided contact channels (grants@bbrfoundation.org) for questions. Check the website for the latest deadlines and guideline versions.
